A mixed F2Cl2 BQ may combine the F-derived margin with the Cl-derived binding and reach f>=2. D14 (Cl4) lost f to a weaker bind (-21.8), so the Cl count is held at two.

edits: replace Cl with F at ring position 2
accepted.hypothesis: D14 (chloranil) has a large margin (0.346) but f is only 0.72 because binding is weak (-21.8). Replacing one Cl with the smaller F should relieve crowding and strengthen binding, as seen for D08 (-24.3) and D07 (-25.8). This should keep the margin above 0.15 and raise f. D11 (Br4) shows that bulkier halogens lower f (0.28), so the change goes to smaller halogens.

Phenanthrenequinone D15 has the strongest binding (-27.9) and f=1.09, but its margin is -0.196. Halogenation raised the margin in D13 over D12 (+0.28) and in D08. Two F on the biphenyl rings should raise the margin toward 0.15 or more while retaining the o-quinone binding mode. Substitution is kept off the dione ring to avoid weakening binding. Risk: ring-remote F may not shift the margin enough. Amino and hydroxy are avoided because they lowered f in D01, D02, D04 and D05.

D07 (2,6-dichloro-BQ) has the highest f (1.24) but its O2 margin is only 0.097. Adding halogens raised the margin in D08 (F4, 0.178, f 1.03) and D14 (Cl4, 0.346, f 0.72). D11 (Br4) raised it further (0.462) but f fell to 0.28, so heavy halogenation costs binding. A single Br is a partial step. It should lift the margin above 0.15 while keeping more of the CO2 binding (D07 bind -25.8) than D14 or D11 did. Promoted: halogenated BQ with no CN, since D07 and D08 raised f and none of the halogenated BQs detached CO2. Avoided: CN (D03, D06, D10 detached CO2) and OH or NH2, which lowered f in D01, D04 and D05. Risk: f may drop toward D14 as halogens are added.

D07 (2,6-dichloro-BQ) is the best-f parent (f=1.24, bind -25.8, no detachment) but its O2 margin is only 0.097. Ring halogenation raised the margin: D08 (F4) 0.178, D14 (Cl4) 0.346, D11 (Br4) 0.462. Heavier halogens cost binding, though (f fell from 1.24 to 0.72 with Cl4 and to 0.28 with Br4), so I add one Br and one F instead of filling the ring with a single heavy halogen. Br should lift the margin above 0.15. F is small and kept strong CO2 binding in D08 (bind -24.3, f=1.03), so it should limit the binding loss. K084 and K029 report CO2 adducts for tetrafluoro-BQ and chloranil, and K058 and K055 show that halogenated BQs stay reducible. I avoided CN (D03, D06, D10 all detached CO2) and NH2/OH (D01, D02, D04, D05 lowered f). This is a promoted-direction test: a mixed F/Cl/Br benzoquinone should combine D07's binding with a margin of at least 0.15. Risk: f may still stay below 2, since no reference reached it, and the margin gain may not offset the binding loss seen from D07 to D14 and D11. DFT will decide.

rejected.hypothesis: D07 (2,6-dichloro-BQ) has the best f of the series (1.24) but its O2 margin is only 0.097. D08 (F4) and D14 (Cl4) show that more ring halogens raise the margin (0.178 and 0.346). Adding two F to D07 should push the margin above 0.15 while keeping the strong CO2 binding that gave the high f. F is small and keeps the binding of D08 (f=1.03). No CN, which detached CO2 in D03, D06 and D10. Risk: f may drop as it did from D07 to D14.

A single F on D07 is a smaller step than the difluoro variant. It should raise the margin from 0.097 toward 0.15 or more while losing less binding than going to Cl4 (f 0.72, bind -21.8). It tests whether a trihalo BQ is the best balance. D07 and D08 both had f>1 with no detachment, so this direction is promoted.

D15 (9,10-phenanthrenequinone) has strong CO2 binding (bind -27.9, f 1.09) and no detachment, but its O2 margin is -0.196. This is similar to AQ (D12, -0.191). Ring chlorination lifted the margin in D13 (0.089 versus D12's -0.191, with f up from 0.14 to 0.38). Cl on the distal rings should therefore raise the margin, and by a larger amount with two Cl. These positions are away from the o-quinone carbonyls, so the binding that gave f 1.09 should be mostly kept. K117 reports an o-quinone CO2 adduct with a very large binding constant (log K 13.06), and K019 reports that 2-Cl-AQ binds CO2. Promoted: halogens on a high-f o-quinone core. Avoided: CN (all detached) and NH2 or OH (D01, D04, D05, D09 all lowered f or the margin). Risk: the margin gain may stay below 0.15, because D13 only reached 0.089.
